clue.text: Carried on board, or stored in hold, depending on circumstances?

definitions.text: Carried on board, or stored in hold, depending on circumstances?

parts.words: Carried on board, or stored in hold, depending on circumstances?
parts.note: a traveller's suitcase goes into the cabin or the hold, whichever suits; the phrase meaning 'depending on circumstances' is read as being about luggage

explanation.surface: Airline advice on where your luggage travels, depending on the situation.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a note about luggage: a case may be carried on board or put in the hold. The stock phrase for 'whichever applies' fits that literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning according to whatever the particular situation turns out to be.

clue.text: Pioneers flying in a country raise toast

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits within the other, here the raising word inside the country

parts.note: land is a general word for a country
to cock something is to raise it, as a dog cocks its ear
to brown bread under the grill is to toast it

explanation.surface: Early aviators, in some nation, lift a glass in celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' looks like a drink to the pioneers but means grilling bread. Alcock and Brown made the first non-stop transatlantic flight in 1919.
explanation.definitionFit: This pair of airmen were aviation pioneers, flying the Atlantic non-stop for the first time.

clue.text: Row about stray dog

indicators.note: about means going round, so the row word is wrapped around the stray word

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats in a stadium
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out over a lost dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests an argument but means a line of seats, a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed of small, energetic dog originally bred for hunting vermin.

clue.text: Game is on TV — fee outrageous

indicators.note: outrageous suggests something wild and out of order, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A viewer complains that a sports broadcast costs an outrageous fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageous' rearranges ISONTVFEE. Eton fives is a handball game played in a walled court, originating at Eton College, the English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a court sport where players strike the ball with gloved hands, a kind of handball.

clue.text: Mobster needs beer having eaten chicken

indicators.note: having eaten means the beer word has taken the chicken word inside it

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table

explanation.surface: A gangster demands beer after his chicken dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster of the Prohibition era, the archetypal mobster.

clue.text: Etna's insides become black, containing cold material thrown out

indicators.note: become says one thing turns into another, so the middle of the volcano's name is swapped for new letters

parts.note: the insides of the word Etna are its middle letters T and N

indicators.note: containing means the black word holds the cold letter inside it

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: The core of the Sicilian volcano turns black, with cold debris blasted out.
explanation.walkthrough: Etna is the Sicilian volcano; 'insides' marks only its middle pair to be replaced, so the outer E and A survive around the new black-and-cold core.
explanation.definitionFit: Ejecta is the volcanic or other matter expelled by an eruption or impact.

clue.text: See 19
See 25
Water thus rising further round end of garden? Wear this

parts.note: water welling up is water rising, as from a spring

indicators.note: round means the further phrase is placed around the garden's last letter

parts.note: to boot means further, in addition

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word garden

explanation.surface: Water is rising further around the garden's end, so what should you put on?
explanation.walkthrough: 'further' is the phrase TO BOOT, opened up by N. The whole clue paints wet ground, and the def 'Wear this' points at the rubber footwear the scene calls for.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber waterproof boots are what you put on your feet for flooded, muddy ground.

clue.text: Anxiety about pet in case of bullets

indicators.note: about means the anxiety word goes around the pet word

parts.note: care is worry or anxiety
to pet an animal is to touch or stroke it

explanation.surface: Someone frets about a pet animal kept near a box of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartouche was historically the paper or wooden case holding a cartridge or bullets.

clue.text: Adult temptation said to subside

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: said tells us the temptation word is heard, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: bait is a lure or temptation

explanation.surface: A grown-up's temptation is said to fade away.
explanation.walkthrough: BATE sounds like BAIT; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: When a storm or pain dies down it lessens, which is the sense of subside here.

clue.text: Richard so named 151 females

parts.note: in Roman numerals 151 is C (100), L (50) and I (1)
F is the abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A man called Richard named 151 women.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff Richard is the veteran British pop singer, so 'Richard so named' is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The British pop star Sir Richard carries this as his stage first name.

clue.text: Latin poet breaking promise

indicators.note: breaking suggests smashing the words apart so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Latin poet fails to keep a promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges LATINPOET; 'promise' is the noun for latent ability, not a vow.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing promise means having the capacity to develop and succeed, latent ability.

clue.text: Four in a Republican cartel reaching destination

indicators.note: in says the number goes inside the cartel word

parts.note: a ring is a group of traders fixing prices, a cartel
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people get inside a Republican price-fixing group.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting to the place one set out for is arrival, so the sense is getting there.

clue.text: Girl lasts in sumo wrestling among island people

indicators.note: among says the picked letters sit within the island-and-people group

parts.note: men means people in general

indicators.note: the lasts in these two words are their final letters

explanation.surface: A girl takes up sumo wrestling with islanders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lasts in' looks like endurance but picks final letters; 'among' puts them inside the island-plus-people pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Imogen is a female given name, the heroine of Shakespeare's Cymbeline.

clue.text: Girl carried round university city

parts.note: Mel is a girl's name, short for Melanie

indicators.note: round means the carried word wraps around the university letter

parts.note: borne means carried

explanation.surface: A girl is carried around a university town.
explanation.definitionFit: Melbourne is the state capital of Victoria in Australia, a large city.

clue.text: Singer very nearly changed name

indicators.note: changed suggests altered form, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A singer very nearly changed her name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very nearly' is not a phrase here: V, then 'changed' rearranges NEARLY into ERALYN. Dame Vera Lynn was the British wartime 'Forces' Sweetheart'.
explanation.definitionFit: She was a celebrated British vocalist, famous for songs sung to troops in the Second World War.

clue.text: Falls down with unknown ailment

parts.note: drops means falls down
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone keeps falling over with a mystery illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropsy is an old name for oedema, a swelling from fluid build-up, so a medical complaint.

clue.text: Assassin perhaps: or one selling shares

parts.note: in slang to off someone is to kill them, so an assassin could be one who offs

explanation.surface: A list asks whether a hitman or a seller of shares is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks a playful coinage: one who offs someone is an OFFER.
explanation.definitionFit: An offeror is the party making an offer, as when a company offers shares for sale.

clue.text: Fortunate encounter an achievement in song 16 made famous

parts.note: well can mean fortunate, as in 'it is well that you came'
to meet is to encounter
a gain is something won or achieved

explanation.surface: A lucky meeting described as a high point in a famous singer's song.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is VERA LYNN, whose 1939 song became the anthem of wartime partings.
explanation.definitionFit: This wartime ballad was the best-known recording by the singer at 16 Down.

clue.text: As one's despicably mean, small tips for servants materialise

indicators.note: despicably suggests bad behaviour, telling us to twist these letters out of order
the tips here are the last letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone is so mean that the servants' tips amount to almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' sounds like gratuities, but with 'for' it picks the final letters of servants and materialise; 'despicably' signals the shuffle of the mean word, and 'one's' hides a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase describes everyone acting together as a single body, all together.

clue.text: Made slow progress: stole quietly away

indicators.note: away tells us the quiet letter is sent off from the stole word

parts.note: pinched means stole
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone crept slowly off having quietly stolen something.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance a little at a time is to creep forward bit by bit, as by a hand's breadth.

clue.text: Arbitrator stopped early and fixed votes

indicators.note: stopped early means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a referee is an arbitrator

indicators.note: fixed, as in a rigged result, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An arbitrator halted the process early and rigged the ballots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped early' drops the final letter of the arbitrator; 'fixed' rearranges the word and, which follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: These are public ballots on a single question, the plural of the Latin-derived term for such a poll.

clue.text: Gets lift in Kalahari desert

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie inside the words Kalahari desert

explanation.surface: A traveller hitches a lift across the Kalahari.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone given a lift in a car is given a ride, so takes rides.

clue.text: Turkish leader invests son in Arab land

indicators.note: invests means clothes or surrounds, so the Arab land wraps round the son letter

parts.note: Oman is an Arab country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A Turkish ruler installs his son in an Arab country.
explanation.definitionFit: Osman I founded the Ottoman dynasty, whose name derives from his.

clue.text: As Johnson spins response misrepresents a right big let-down

indicators.note: misrepresents means giving a false picture, so these letters are presented in a new order

explanation.surface: Political commentary: the Prime Minister's spin hides a massive disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson, as UK Prime Minister, promised a 'world-beating' Covid test-and-trace system; 'misrepresents' rearranges A, R, BIG and LETDOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the boastful claim of being the best on earth, Johnson's signature hype.

clue.text: Here to spy producing tricky words?

indicators.note: producing, as a conjuror produces from a hat, brings these letters out in a new order

explanation.surface: A spy hides behind clever wording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' rearranges HERETOSPY; 'tricky words' are a magician's, said as the trick is revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror says this exclamation at the moment a trick reaches its surprise.

clue.text: Drunken client pestered one coming into office

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tipsy customer harassed a newly arriving official.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of someone who has won a presidential vote but not yet taken up the post.
